Topics · Hard times

How can a good God allow children to suffer?

No complete answer is claimed. The text raises it, complaint is allowed, and the child's question stands.

If you are in pain right now, you do not have to carry it alone. Please reach out to someone you trust, or to a local crisis line or emergency number. Find a helpline near you

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً ۖ قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ ۖ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [mention, O Muḥammad], when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority."[17] They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with praise and declare Your perfection?"[18] He [Allāh] said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know."

Translator's notes

[17] Khalīfah: successor, or generations of man, one following another. [18] An additional meaning is "...and we purify ourselves for You."

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:30

Translation

One called to another, and said, “Holy, holy, holy, is Yahweh of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!”

Original · Hebrew

וְקָרָ֨א זֶ֤ה אֶל־זֶה֙ וְאָמַ֔ר קָד֧וֹשׁ ׀ קָד֛וֹשׁ קָד֖וֹשׁ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת מְלֹ֥א כָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ כְּבוֹדֽוֹ׃

Isaiah · 6:3

World English Bible

No one who has sat beside a sick child should be given a neat answer, and none is offered. The question is older than any critic. In this verse, it is the angels who ask: will You put there those who will spread ruin and shed blood? The reply is not a theory. It is: I know what you do not know. That may sound like no answer, and to someone in pain that is fair. It does show the question is not forbidden. It is in the book.

A question for you

What is closest to what you bring to this question?

If you sayA personal pain.
ThenThen you do not need an argument now. You may stop here. This page has one more thing for you: complaint is allowed.
If you sayAn objection to a good God existing.
ThenThat is a serious objection, and no one here claims to defeat it.
If you sayAnger at those who justify this.
ThenThat anger is understandable. This app never tells a person in pain that their suffering is a test or a punishment.

the Psalms · 142:1-3

World English Bible

﴿وَأَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [mention] Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful."

Quran · Al-Anbiya 21:83

Translation

Yahweh restored Job’s prosperity when he prayed for his friends. Yahweh gave Job twice as much as he had before.

Original · Hebrew

וַֽיהוָ֗ה שָׁ֚ב אֶת־שְׁב֣וּת אִיּ֔וֹב בְּהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֖וֹ בְּעַ֣ד רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַ֧יֹּסֶף יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאִיּ֖וֹב לְמִשְׁנֶֽה׃

Job · 42:10

World English Bible

Whatever else is true, this much is in the text: a person in pain may say so to God, directly. A father overwhelmed by loss says that he takes his grief and sorrow to God. A man struck by affliction says that harm has touched him. Neither is told to be quiet, or to explain it away, or to be grateful. Both men speak to God, not against Him. If your own words are harder, no one here will silence them.

A question for you

Does it change anything that complaint is allowed?

If you sayA little. I didn't know.
ThenMany were told the opposite. That is enough for now.
If you sayNo. I don't want to complain, I want an answer.
ThenThat is a fair demand. What comes next is as far as honesty can go.
If you sayI don't think there is anyone to complain to.
ThenThat is your view. The suffering stays real, and so does the protest.

Quran · At-Takwir 81:8-9

﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ لَا تُقَـٰتِلُونَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ وَٱلنِّسَآءِ وَٱلْوِلْدَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَخْرِجْنَا مِنْ هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلظَّالِمِ أَهْلُهَا وَٱجْعَل لَّنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِيًّا وَٱجْعَل لَّنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ نَصِيرًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And what is [the matter] with you that you fight not in the cause of Allāh and [for] the oppressed among men, women and children who say, "Our Lord, take us out of this city of oppressive people and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper"?

Quran · An-Nisa 4:75

Translation

Open your mouth for the mute, in the cause of all who are left desolate. Open your mouth, judge righteously, and serve justice to the poor and needy.”

Original · Hebrew

פְּתַח־פִּ֥יךָ לְאִלֵּ֑ם אֶל־דִּ֝֗ין כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י חֲלֽוֹף׃ פְּתַח־פִּ֥יךָ שְׁפָט־צֶ֑דֶק וְ֝דִ֗ין עָנִ֥י וְאֶבְיֽוֹן׃

Proverbs · 31:8-9

World English Bible

This is as far as it goes. The text does not say the child's pain is worth it. It does two other things. It keeps the child's case open: a buried girl is asked, at the end, for what offence she was killed. And it turns to those able to act: what is wrong with you, that you do not fight for the helpless, children among them? No complete answer to the suffering of children is known. Refusing to make peace with a child's pain is not a fault.

A question for you

Where does this leave you?

If you sayIt isn't enough. I don't accept such a world.
ThenThat is a serious moral position, and it is not corrected here.
If you sayI don't understand, but I am not throwing everything out.
ThenMany live there, and no one asks more of you.
If you sayI want to know why there is a test at all.
ThenThat is a whole question of its own, and it has its limits.

The same in the other books
